title: A Release for This Vehicle: Only When It Is Parked and Charged, Never With Another Vehicle's Calibration, and Kept Only If It Drives Properly

questions.question: Why is an update refused when the vehicle is not parked?
options: The download needs the vehicle's radio
The battery charges only when parked
The new release needs a fresh calibration drive
It is a reboot, and a reboot of a moving vehicle is a stop and a lost mission
questions.explanation: Installing means restarting. Restarting a moving vehicle stops it where it is and loses its place in the mission.

questions.question: A vehicle that was moving, in a mission and at 20 percent charge was refused for how many reasons?
questions.explanation: Not parked, a mission under way and charge under 50 percent. All are listed, so a person sees the whole of it and not only the first.

questions.question: A track width of 0.40 m taken for 0.25 m makes a skid steer turn:
questions.explanation: 0.40 over 0.25 is 1.60. The software thinks the tracks are closer together than they are and asks for too little difference between them.

questions.question: A release that failed its self test was rolled back after how many boots?
questions.explanation: It gets three tries. On the boot after they are used up the boot loader goes back to the old slot.

questions.question: What does only a self test pass do?
options: Marks the old slot as bad
questions.explanation: After the update the vehicle drives a short test on the new software. Only passing that confirms it; saying it is healthy is not enough.

questions.question: Why is a charge that is not a number counted as low?
options: A comparison with it is false, so it must fail the check
A battery with no reading is always flat
To make the update take longer
Because the charge is a block and not a warning
questions.explanation: The check is written as charge at least the minimum. A value that is not a number makes that false, which is the safe way for it to fall.
